shots.name: 1 · Extreme wide set
shots.purpose: establishing: the open ground and the direction of escape
shots.why: The establishing frame answers 'where are we' so every later close-up can be placed in space. The high camera diminishes and surveils; the subject looks smaller and more exposed. Leading the escaper on a wide lens puts the audience in their effort; the look back keeps the unseen pursuit alive without showing it. The long-lens wide that lets them disappear is the payoff: distance itself becomes the escape. Rule: establish the start point and the destination direction in one wide before going close, because speed only reads against a known space; inserts without geography are just noise.
alternatives: Avoid cutting between shots where the runners travel opposite screen directions: it reads as a reversal or a second chase.
Hold it longer than feels comfortable if the scene needs more weight; wides earn their duration.
